title: Clinical Documentation Standard: Compliance Downloads as Proof of Continued Use for the PAP Supply Replenishment Program
content:
## Clinical documentation standard

For the PAP Supply Replenishment Program, proof of continued use is read from the patient's PAP device record, as follows.

1. **The newest download.** The newest compliance download on the device record proves continued use when all three hold: its average daily use reaches the device class's compliance minimum hours; its window holds the device class's full compliance window of nights; and the device class's compliance night percentage of those nights reach four hours of use (the nights with four or more hours, taken as a share of the nights in the window, are at least that percentage). It is then credited at the last night of its window.
2. **A download that falls short.** A newest download that falls short of any of these is set aside for the newest download that met the device class's compliance standard (recorded on the device record as having met it), credited at the last night of its window.
3. **Kind of proof the schedule accepts.** On a schedule that accepts either compliance data or a practitioner note, the newer of that credited download date and the visit date of the newest practitioner re-evaluation documenting benefit is recorded. A schedule that accepts only one kind records the newest proof of its own kind: the credited download date where it accepts compliance data only, the visit date of the newest re-evaluation documenting benefit where it accepts a practitioner note only.
4. **Comparison with the enrollment.** The date reached is recorded on the enrollment only when it is newer than the enrollment's continued-use date; otherwise the enrollment's date stays. Where the device record holds neither a qualifying download nor a re-evaluation documenting benefit, no date is reached and the enrollment's date stays.

The device class's compliance minimum hours, full compliance window and compliance night percentage are the figures of the device's class under PAP Therapy Equipment.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

Device class figures: 4.0 hours minimum, a 30-night window, 70 percent of nights at four hours. Newest download: average 4.6 hours, 30 nights in its window, 22 nights at four hours or more, last night of its window on the 10th of a month. Twenty-two nights are about 73 percent of 30, at least 70 percent; 4.6 hours reaches 4.0; 30 nights reach 30. The download proves continued use and is credited at the 10th. On a schedule that accepts either kind, with the newest re-evaluation documenting benefit dated the 2nd of the same month, the newer date is the 10th. If the enrollment's continued-use date is earlier than the 10th, the 10th is recorded.

*Variation:* had the same download shown only 19 nights at four hours (about 63 percent), it would fall short and be set aside for the newest download recorded as meeting the standard, credited at the last night of that download's window.
